name: Risograph
summary: Stencil-printed animation: two or three translucent spot inks (Riso blue, yellow, fluorescent pink) overprinting on warm paper, stepped halftone bands instead of gradients, grainy streaky ink, plates that never quite line up, and heavy grotesque titles printed on one plate or double-hit on two.
suits: small figure in a big world
something new arrives (one plate per turning point)

palette.use: warm off-white paper: knockouts, highlights, the caption strip (never pure white)
Riso blue, plate 1 (screen 15°): type, silhouettes, the one-ink plate
fluorescent pink, plate 3 (screen 75°): double-hits, emphasis, ground
the 38% blue tint as a flat colour, for UI that can't halftone
the 20% blue tint as a flat colour

type.case: titles uppercase; headlines and captions sentence case
type.emphasis: a second plate: the emphasised word prints on pink, or double-hits pink + blue 10 px apart

banned: flat vector art with a noise overlay: every colour comes from the plates
CMYK pop-art halftone: no process colours, no keylines
screen-print poster looks: riso ink is translucent and grainy
the RISO brand, logo or machine trade dress (ink names are colour references only)
more than 3 inks; three halftoned plates in one area
registration jitter or streaks that change every frame
cross-dissolves, soft digital wipes and fading titles
saturated dots on skin; pure white paper
copying a named illustrator's characters, compositions or palettes
